title: Time-slice yield controller for KV-aware GPU memory coordination
creator: Aisha Park
description: Problem: Continuous batching currently uses coarse preemption and binary eviction decisions that can cause noisy neighbor effects when tenants hold large KV caches or when GPU memory becomes fragmented. This leads to oscillating latencies and tail SLO violations for low-latency tenants during high load. Goal: implement a 'time-slice yield controller' that (1) enforces SLO-aware time slices per request group, (2) coordinates soft-yield semantics with KV slab reservation and KV eviction prioritization, and (3) performs GPU memory compaction-friendly reclamation rather than abrupt full-reclaims. The controller should integrate with the runtime's scheduler and KV manager to make preemption decisions that prefer fairness and SLO preservation rather than aggressive throughput maximization.
acceptance_criteria: New controller integrated into continuous batcher runtime and configurable via runtime config (timeout and slice size)
Measured 95th percentile token latency for P0 SLO tenants improves under mixed load vs current preemption baseline (>=10% reduction in tail during synthetic hotspots)

KV slab accounting is respected: controller can reserve a configurable min-resident slab per tenant and will use soft-yield to avoid evicting below that slab unless tenant is over commit for > grace period
GPU memory reclamation performs in increments to avoid fragmentation spikes; memory compaction hooks executed as fallback and no OOM during standard load tests
E2E tests and integration tests added covering: (a) tenant time-slice enforcement, (b) soft-yield + KV reservation interplay, (c) emergency hard-reclaim path
Telemetry emitted: per-tenant slice utilization, preemption_count, soft_yield_events, kv_eviction_count, memory_compaction_events
design_notes: We previously relied on abrupt preemption that requeues entire requests and immediately evicts KV items when reclaim needed. That approach reduces throughput but causes tail latency spikes for low-latency tenants. The controller introduces a time-slice model: each scheduling window (configurable, e.g., 10ms) grants a tenant a token-budget or CPU/compute-time fraction. When a tenant's slice expires, the runtime will attempt compact soft-yielding: checkpoint minimal kernel state, flush any optional caches to prefix cache storage, and enqueue the remainder at the back of the ready queue. For KV-aware behavior we add three levers: (1) min_resident_slab - small reserved KV footprint per tenant (default 8MB) that is protected from automatic eviction during soft-yield; (2) age-and-frequency eviction priority that biases out cold KV segments before hot ones; (3) staged eviction where we attempt quick slab eviction increments before triggering a hard reclaim. To coordinate GPU memory compaction, we leverage the allocator's free-list coalescing path and avoid freeing large contiguous blocks in one shot; instead use a staged release that signals the memory manager to merge neighboring free regions. The controller exposes a compatibility shim for older schedulers and a metrics facade for Console dashboards.
implementation_plan: RFC: finalize API between scheduler and kv-manager (2d)
Add time-slice bookkeeping to batcher core (3d)
Implement soft-yield mechanics: state checkpoint, enqueue rest-of-request path (4d)
KV manager: add min_resident_slab, staged-eviction APIs and telemetry (5d)
GPU allocator: add staged-release hooks and compaction signals (3d)
Integration: wire controller to routing policies and expose runtime config flags (2d)
Add unit/integration tests and synthetic load harnesses (4d)
testing_plan: Unit tests for slice accounting and soft-yield path
Integration tests that simulate mixed SLO tenants with KV-heavy and CPU-heavy workloads
Chaos tests: force memory pressure and verify graceful staged reclaim without crashing
A/B performance test in staging comparing existing preemption vs yield controller under 3 workload mixes
Telemetry validation: ensure per-tenant metrics flow to Console and correlate with logs
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag `time_slice_yield_v1`. Start with canary on dedicated pool (internal infra only) for 48h with synthetic traffic. If metrics stable, enable in staging across 10% of hosts for one week. Gradual ramp to 50% across runtime clusters with monitoring for tail latency regressions. For customers with strict KV requirements, expose min_resident_slab override in Dedicated/Private configs. Rollback path: disable flag and revert to previous preemption controller; ensure graceful draining before rollback completes.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Controller may increase average latency due to extra enqueueing overhead. Mitigation: tune slice size and implement an adaptive slice that grows/shrinks based on observed utilization.

Risk: Incorrect KV slab reservation could cause overall memory overcommit. Mitigation: clamp total reserved slab budget per host and surface warnings in Console; fall back to hard-reclaim once host-level pressure exceeds threshold.
Risk: Memory compaction hooks may interact poorly with third-party allocator. Mitigation: keep compaction optional and guarded by feature flag; preflight test on allocator variants.
Risk: Telemetry volume increase. Mitigation: sample soft-yield events at 10% by default and allow customers to turn on full sampling for debug.
